body: Beautiful illustration of romance. Coming of age story for those of us who don't have a mainstream story. Not just for gay men, or bikers, or those with sub/dom desires. This is a story of someone finding themself, someone who can't share themself, parents who are supportive even if they don't get it. It's sexy and funny and romantic. Giving a 10 bc what am i grading it against? Until we get thousands of movies over 100 years to compare it to, (like str8 love stories) i can't say it's anything but perfect. No need for straight ppl to watch or approve. 10/10.

I was surprised when the local cinema chain decided to show this movie, simply because of the subject mater. As a gay man of a certain age and inclination, I found much of the movie relatable, and I can see why younger generations wouldn't understand it quite as much.

This look at the MC sub-culture that was especially present in the later years of the 20th century was interesting. The cinematography was excellent, and it was an interesting mix of 21st century ideals (especially from the parents being so supportive of their son's sexual orientation), conflicting with rather Old Guard values in the gay BDSM culture.

I found the movie to be brilliant, even if there were a couple of gaps in the story that I had to figure out along the way.

Definitely not a movie for everyone, and it shouldn't be, but I found it a compelling film.

I liked this movie. Even when it crossed the line and went full gay porn at times, I didn't feel disgusted or tempted to look away. And I think that's exactly the director's skill - showing things that aren't meant to please everyone, without apologizing for them.

It's not subtle or delicate. Sometimes it's rough, even confrontational. But it still felt right - at least for me. Honest, exposed, unapologetic. And honestly, I keep noticing the same thing over and over: the most romantic films - or at least the ones that feel the most romantic - are almost always gay movies. Why is that?

When I learned Adam Mars-Jones' Box Hill was being adapted into a romantic comedy, I was baffled because the novel contains very little typical romance or comedy. Instead, it has plenty of heartbreak and loss. But Harry Lighton's script builds on the source material in an extraordinary way: he moves the story from the 1970s to the modern day, makes Ray American, and avoids the novel's very dramatic ending, instead leaning into a coming-of-age story, which brings out comedy and sweetness of the relationship. This version gives Colin dignity. He finds himself and establishes his boundaries. Colin's parents are given a unique arc: they start as supportive parents of their son's sexuality, but throughout the film they are less accepting of Colin and Ray's relationship.

The last shot of Ray will stick with me for a while. Absolutely loved it.

Pillion is a fascinating glimpse into a world that isn't often explored in film, centering around the BDSM relationship between commanding biker Ray and his timid new submissive Colin.

Perhaps strangely, it makes for a deeply moving and involving story of love and lust and control and identity. It presents a really fresh perspective on these themes and how relationships exist in different forms but boil down to the same basic wants and needs. It's a masterfully worked script, using silence and physicality alongside measured dialogue to convey the full spectrum of human emotion. Narratively it maybe lacks a bit of drive in places, but the emotional arcs involved keep the momentum going.

Harry Melling and Alexander Skarsgard deliver two powerhouse performances at complete opposite ends of the spectrum, yet strangely similar too. Both men are mild mannered and of few words, yet they hide so much behind their exteriors and both men convey these layers so well. The chemistry they had was electric and tense and tender and so interesting to watch develop and unfold.

Stylistically I thought the film was great. It was quite spartan in its approach, nice and clean and refined, and had a lovely score that complimented everything so well.

As a final note, in case you are of a delicate persuasion, this film does not leave much to the imagination. If the thought of a gay BSDM relationship is even moderately uncomfortable to you, this film won't be for you as it does not shy away from what that entails!

Ultimately I thought this film was brilliant. The characters are beautifully sketched out and performed so well, and the emotional arc of the relationship is so interesting and compelling. A fantastic piece of cinema!
